summary: PJM files a partial compliance filing under the June 18, 2026 co-location rehearing and paper hearing order, adding Eligible Load, Interim NITS in new Tariff Part XI and Necessary Study rules, while deferring contract demand services and BTMG netting to a later filing.
ask: Accept the Tariff revisions effective October 17, 2026, except new Part XI for Interim NITS, which PJM asks to make effective July 1, 2028 with waiver of the 120-day filing limit.

points.point: PJM files under FPA section 206 to comply with the June 18 order and plans a full section 205 large load filing by mid-November.
points.quote: PJM intends to submit that filing by mid-November 2026.

points.point: PJM sets October 17, 2026 for most revisions and July 1, 2028 for Interim NITS so it can build tools to curtail non-firm service.
points.quote: PJM proposes an effective date of July 1, 2028, to provide time for operational changes and implementation of additional operational tools

points.point: PJM adds an Eligible Load definition covering co-located load and load behind BTMG, so both can take Interim NITS.
points.quote: Eligible Load shall mean Co-Located Load or load connected to Behind the Meter Generation.

points.point: PJM removes the 50 MW nameplate limit from the Retail BTMG definition, as the June order directed, and works on the 50 MW netting materiality threshold separately.
points.quote: eliminates the rejected 50 MW nameplate limit and other netting exemptions

points.point: Customers must pass the Necessary Study process and finish upgrades before serving co-located load, from existing or new generators.
points.quote: not begin serving Eligible Load until the entire scope of the work under their GIA as amended after the Necessary Study process is complete.

points.point: Customers with existing service agreements can modify them through the Necessary Study process rather than sign a new GIA.
points.quote: PJM is proposing changes to allow customers that obtained service agreements pursuant to Parts VI and VII to modify those agreements

points.point: Interim NITS is energy-only and non-firm, converts to NITS once upgrades are done, and is suspended for up to 120 days after a first dispatch failure.
points.quote: suspend service for up to 120 days after the first instance and terminate service after the second.

points.point: PJM defers Firm and Non-Firm Contract Demand services and some BTMG netting to a later compliance filing under a 90-day extension.
points.quote: PJM sought a 90-day extension of certain directives in the June Order.

throughLine.text: Carries out the E-2 co-location order's directives on Interim NITS, Eligible Load and BTMG netting, and ties its timing to PJM's larger E-7 large load response due mid-November.

figures.label: Retail BTMG netting materiality threshold in the June order
figures.quote: permit Retail BTMG netting up to a 50 MW materiality threshold
